transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-14
Time: 09:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Park (Redwood Solutions), Elena Ruiz (BlueFin CTO), Samir Khan (BlueFin Dev Lead), Priya Mehta (BlueFin Head of Security), Jake Turner (BlueFin SRE)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery to map integration touchpoints.

00:00 Elena: Okay everyone thanks for joining from BlueFin uh we basically want to understand how Redwood would slot into our architecture for the new customer insights product.
00:12 Maya: Great thanks Elena really appreciate it. I'll let Raj do the deep technical bits but quick overview from us: Redwood provides hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and a Private VPC/on-prem control plane. Today we want to surface SDKs, LangChain support, gateway patterns, and observability hooks.
00:28 Raj: Hey everyone, yeah hi, Samir, Priya, Jake — quick question, what's your current stack for inference? Are you using any managed API today?
00:36 Samir: We're using a mix. For prototypes we've used OpenAI, and some internal TF models but for production we have a self-hosted transformer pipeline behind an internal gateway. Latency's okay but costs are spiky and we hit throughput limits during end-of-month runs.
00:52 Priya: Security wise we need audit logs, KMS integration for keys, and we have a SAML SSO. Data residency is a must for EU customers.
01:04 Raj: Got it. On the SDK side — Redwood has first-party SDKs for Python, Node, and go — uh go is experimental — and we publish LangChain connectors and LlamaIndex integration snippets.
01:18 Olivia: When you say LangChain connectors, is that official or community?
01:22 Maya: Official connectors maintained by Redwood — examples show chains, agents, retriever setup using our embeddings endpoints and also caching patterns. They include LlamaIndex examples too though some names in docs are Llama... Llama index (lami index) sometimes transcribed wrong in older docs but the code works.
01:38 Samir: Do you have an example for long context with prefix caching / KV cache? We need to keep session memory for 20k tokens for some workflows.
01:48 Raj: Yes we support KV cache and prefix caching at the runtime. For hosted we do automatic KV caching with a TTL and memory-aware eviction, for Dedicated you can pin model variants and we expose the cache control APIs. Note: those APIs are in beta for the hosted public plane — for dedicated they're GA.
02:04 Jake: On network topology, can you describe the gateway pattern? Our infra team wants a thin proxy gateway that handles auth and rate limits closer to our prod ingress.
02:14 Raj: Common pattern is customer gateway/proxy on your side that terminates SSO and enforces per-customer quotas then forwards to Redwood's edge gateway. For Private we run the control plane inside your VPC so calls stay internal; for Dedicated you can set up a VPC peering and a private endpoint.
02:29 Priya: So if we go Dedicated we still need to send tokens across peering? What's encrypted and what stays in our VPC?
02:36 Maya: With Private you get the control plane on your VPC and you can keep data within your network; with Dedicated there's options for private endpoints and TLS across peering; payloads are encrypted in transit and at rest. We also integrate with customer KMS for key management when requested.
02:49 Elena: What about SLOs — we need 99th percentile latency under 200ms for short prompts. Is that realistic?
02:56 Raj: For short generation prompts on dedicated GPU pools that's doable depending on the model and sequence length. On hosted there are more multi-tenant patterns, but we expose performance profiles. We can run a benchmark POC to measure p99 for your queries.
03:10 Samir: Ok, benchmarks would be ideal. Also about SDKs — do you have LangChain agents that can call external tools and then pass tool output to the model?
03:20 Raj: Yes, the LangChain connector includes tool calling examples and streaming responses. Note streaming currently has subtle differences across runtime modes — streaming chunk sizes and flush behavior will vary slightly between hosted and dedicated.
03:34 Speaker 1: (faint) does Redwood support function calling?
03:37 Maya: Yes function or tool calling is supported, though the signed schema enforcement in Private deployments is stricter by default.
03:46 Priya: Observability — we need traces and per-request tokens breakdown for cost allocation. Can we hook our tracing and log aggregation?
03:55 Raj: Absolutely — we expose tracing hooks (OpenTelemetry), request IDs in headers, and per-token billing metadata in the response headers/body for observability. We also export Prometheus metrics for throughput, latencies, cache hit rates, and token counts.
04:10 Jake: Do you provide example dashboards or Grafana dashboards to onboard SREs?
04:14 Olivia: Yes we have reference dashboards and dashboards templates. We can share a Grafana dashboard JSON.
04:20 Elena: Rate limits and quotas — we have a multi-tenant product, so we need per-customer quotas and burst allowances. How granular are Redwood quotas?
04:30 Raj: Quotas can be set per API key, per route, and per tenant with both steady-state and burst windows. There's also token-based and request-count-based limits. For Dedicated you can request higher throughput and set custom throttles at the edge gateway.
04:45 Samir: If we set a high burst for end of month, does that impact noisy neighbor issues on hosted?
04:51 Maya: On hosted multi-tenant, yes bursts are subject to pool availability and fairness policies; Dedicated avoids noisy neighbors. You can also configure fallback policies so if capacity is constrained requests route to a cheaper model variant or queue.
05:06 Priya: Compliance — SOC2, ISO, audit logs — do you have a compliance pack?
05:10 Maya: We have a security package with SOC2 documentation, ISO attestation, and audit log exports. For Private we can increase retention and provide custom audit endpoints.
05:19 Elena: On costs — we need unit economics. Can you show cost per 1k tokens on hosted vs dedicated? Also, how does quantization reduce cost?
05:30 Raj: We'll send a model/quantization recommendation. Roughly quantized model variants (e.g., 4-bit) reduce GPU memory and increase throughput; that translates into lower per-token cost on Dedicated. We'll include example pricing and sample throughput numbers in the follow-up.
05:44 Samir: For our stack we use LangChain with a local retriever and LlamaIndex for documents. Any gotchas?
05:51 Raj: The common gotchas are: ensure retriever vectors use the same embedding dimension and that you batch embed calls for efficiency; use our embeddings endpoint which supports batching. For LlamaIndex we show sample wrappers. Also watch out for rate limit retries in the chain — exponential backoff recommended.
06:08 Elena: Timeline — we're aiming for a Q4 launch with an internal pilot in 6 weeks. Is that feasible?
06:15 Maya: Yes, a 1-week POC for benchmarking and an additional 4 weeks for integration is a common cadence. We'd propose POC kickoff next week pending paperwork.
06:24 Priya: On the paperwork — we need DPIA + data flow diagrams for Private deployment.
06:29 Maya: We'll send the compliance artifacts and a template DPIA.
06:33 Jake: Can we test a local gateway -> Redwood edge flow with simulated traffic?
06:39 Raj: Definitely — we'll provide a test harness and a sample proxy config.
06:43 Elena: Anything else on rate limits, quotas? I want to ensure billing is split per customer.
06:49 Maya: We can include per-tenant sub-keys and token accounting metadata for downstream billing.
06:55 Samir: One more question — do you have examples of LangChain agents that use retrieval augmented generation with caching across sessions?
07:01 Raj: Yes, we have a pattern in the docs using persistent KV + embedding caches; often we combine a local vector DB (e.g., we show Pinecone and FAISS examples) with our embeddings endpoint and a sticky session for KV.
07:16 Elena: Ok good. Let's recap next steps.
07:20 Maya: Recap: we'll send integration guide + LangChain/LlamaIndex snippets, benchmark config, hosted vs dedicated pricing, compliance pack (SOC2/ISO/DPIA template), and a Grafana dashboard template. BlueFin will confirm compliance items and pick a POC model and representative prompts.
07:38 Priya: I'll compile compliance list and share by Thursday.
07:42 Samir: We'll identify 3 benchmark prompts and traffic profile by Friday.
07:47 Maya: Great — I'll follow up with calendar invites for POC kickoff and a technical deep-dive on VPC networking.
07:52 Elena: Thanks everyone.
07:55 Maya: Thanks all.

(End of transcript)
